reason: Prior K-loop experiments passed correctness but did not earn promotion, and their noisy results do not establish which scheduling ideas help. I rank the distinct register-use and pointer-update schedules first because they keep the packing layout, tile traversal, and output mapping intact; prefetch is next, with a guarded final iteration and no established locality benefit. Store-order changes have greater row-mapping risk, while grouped stores and direct ZA stores need exact assembler support that the supplied evidence does not establish. The compact A-panel proposals under a_transpose and cache_blocking describe substantially the same packing and scratch change; do not treat both as separate tests. The B-panel proposals also overlap, and B is already loaded contiguously. Cache-conflict padding has the weakest evidence: cache sizes do not establish a conflict bottleneck, and padding adds scratch traffic. All expected benefits are hypotheses, not measured facts.
